intro: A cup of iced chocolate from a café is about 380 kcal (estimate). Most of it comes from full cream milk, chocolate sauce and the whipped cream on top.
diet: Yes, but it's closer to a dessert than a normal drink. 380 kcal is about the same as a small plate of nasi lemak. Enjoy it now and then when you lepak at a café. If you have one, cut back on other snacks or desserts that day.
tips: Ask for no whipped cream to save about 70 kcal.
Pick the smallest size or share with a friend.
Ask for 'less sweet' or low-fat milk if the café offers it.

swap.name: Iced latte, no sugar
swap.why: Still has milk and protein, minus the chocolate sauce and whipped cream. Saves over 200 kcal.

faq.a: A little from the cocoa, but far less than coffee. Good if you want to avoid coffee.

faq.q: Is iced chocolate okay for kids?
faq.a: Yes, as an occasional treat. Go for a small, less sweet version since the sugar is quite high.

faq.q: What's the difference between iced chocolate and Milo ais?
faq.a: Café iced chocolate usually uses chocolate sauce and fresh milk, sometimes with whipped cream. Mamak Milo ais uses Milo powder with condensed or evaporated milk.
